draft.title: The Declaration of the Rights of Man
card: The National Assembly passed the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen in August 1789. It set out the principles the new France would be built on.
people have natural rights, such as freedom of speech and freedom from arbitrary arrest. Liberty is limited only by the rights of others.
the law is the same for everyone, and public office is open to people on merit, not birth. This ended the idea that nobles and commoners are judged differently.
final authority belongs to the nation, not to the king. The king's power now came from the people and the law.
draft.remember: The declaration put rights and the nation above birth and the king.

a.q: Which idea in the declaration challenged the king's claim to rule by his own right?
a.why: Sovereignty of the nation placed final authority in the nation, so the king's power came from the people and the law. Equality before the law is tempting, but it is about how people are treated by the law, not about who holds final authority.
a.clue: Think about who holds final authority.

b.q: In 1790 a court in Lyon gives a noble and a baker the same punishment for the same theft. Which principle of the declaration does this show?
b.why: The same law is applied to both people whatever their birth, which is equality before the law. Liberty from arbitrary arrest is tempting, but the case is about equal treatment, not about being detained without lawful reason.
b.clue: Focus on the noble and the baker receiving the same treatment.
